subject: ENG-205
topic: Beowulf Part 2 (Another Attack to Another Celebration at Heorot)

cards.def: A lake or pool, especially a dark and marshy one.
The poet calls her a "monstrous hell-bride," "hell-dam," "roaming killer," "troll-dam," "wolfish swimmer," "swamp-thing from hell," "tarn-hag," and "wolf of the deep."
Part 2 uses "heather-stepper" for a hart, "sail-road" and "gannet's bath" for the sea, "bone-cage" for the body, "battle-torch" for a sword, and "heaven's candle" for the sun.
A "rare and ancient sword" whose iron blade, with its "ill-boding patterns," had been "tempered in blood" and had never failed anyone who carried it into battle (around line 1458).
An old Irish word for a learned judge or lawgiver, which Heaney uses as a title for Unferth.
Hrothgar's phrase for growing wise by living through many hard winters (around line 1725).
Giving human actions or feelings to something that is not human, as when a wood "waits and keeps watch."
